input:
If ∫ dx/(x √(1-x³)) = k log( (√(1-x³) - 1) / (√(1-x³) + 1) ) + c, (where c is a constant of integration), then value of k is

Options:
A. 2/3
B. -2/3
C. 1/3
D. -1/3

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the indefinite integral ∫ dx/(x √(1-x³)) to find the constant coefficient k in the log expression.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Multiply numerator and denominator by x² to get ∫ x² dx / (x³ √(1-x³)). Substitute 1 - x³ = t² so that -3x² dx = 2t dt.

key_concepts: Derivative: -3x² dx = 2t dt ⇒ x² dx = -2t dt / 3
Standard log integral formula: ∫ dt / (t² - 1) = (1/2) log |(t - 1) / (t + 1)| + c

key_formulas.substitution: 1 - x³ = t²  ⇒  x³ = 1 - t², x² dx = (-2/3) t dt

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Rewrite integrand as x²/(x³ √(1-x³)), substitute t = √(1-x³), evaluate the resulting standard integral, and compare coefficients to find k.
logical_steps: Step 1: Multiply top and bottom by x²: I = ∫ x² dx / (x³ √(1-x³))
Step 2: Let 1 - x³ = t² ⇒ x³ = 1 - t² and x² dx = (-2/3) t dt
Step 3: Substitute: I = ∫ [(-2/3) t dt] / [(1 - t²) t] = (2/3) ∫ dt / (t² - 1)
Step 6: Substitute back t = √(1-x³) and deduce k = 1/3, matching option C

step_2_substitution.differential: -3x² dx = 2t dt  ⇒  x² dx = (-2/3) t dt

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: After substitution 1-x³ = t², integral equals (2/3) ∫ dt/(t²-1) = (1/3) log|(t-1)/(t+1)| + c. Comparing with k log(...) gives k = 1/3 ✓
